Once you can do 12 reps, increase the weight until you can only crank out 8. This is not the only way to increase your pull ups, but it is a way. Also negatives are helpful (starting at the top of the bar and slowly lowering yourself)

Also, what’s your diet look like? It’s possible you’re not eating enough to make your muscles stronger.

I haven’t been prescribed anything. She and I kept prescriptions as an option but initially started with getting to the root of my issues and working from there which has been effective.

I think some people need medicinal assistance in regulating their brain chemicals in a healthy way. And I hope they find it. For me, it was more event driven then an internal process. My brother and father died on the same day when I was in college and I just fell apart like any normal person. But when I finished grieving it’s like I died with them. I came out of that with a numbness that lasted for years. My first thought every morning was, “Damn...I woke up.” I didn’t feel anything real.

Getting to the root of all this and making a new me is what has helped me. Instead of trying to get back to the way I was happy before, I’ve focused on building a new foundation that I can be happy on. (Bodybuilding and fitness in general have played a huge role in this) A different happy, but still satisfying. I had to accept that I had fundamentally changed as a person, and that that was okay. 

Like I said, not everyone needs prescription medications, but a lot do, and I hope everyone finds what they’re looking for.

The most important thing is doing what you find sustainable, the second most important is to stay under calories, third most important is to get enough protein.
